name: 35. Gemini/Vertex googleSearch grounding filters + retrievalConfig (/genai)
description:
Google Search grounding fields on the /genai route that had zero harness coverage: googleSearch.excludeDomains, googleSearch.timeRangeFilter (both camelCase and snake_case), and toolConfig.retrievalConfig.latLng on the request side, plus groundingMetadata fidelity on the response side for both non-streaming and streaming.

The /genai route is NOT passthrough: the request crosses Gemini JSON -> BifrostResponsesRequest -> Gemini JSON, and the response crosses back the same way. Every one of these fields therefore has two chances to be silently dropped, and a dropped field still returns 200 - the model just quietly runs an unfiltered search. So the assertions are on response content, not status:

- excludeDomains / timeRangeFilter / retrievalConfig.latLng have no distinctive response signature, so they are pinned by the fact that the provider accepts them AND still grounds. A mangled or misnamed field is a 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT from Google; a dropped tool means no groundingMetadata at all.
- excludeDomains is Vertex-only - the Gemini Developer API does not accept it - so every case carrying it runs on Vertex alone. timeRangeFilter and retrievalConfig.latLng run on both.
- The latLng cases additionally assert no functionCallingConfig was synthesized: Gemini rejects functionCallingConfig without function declarations, so rebuilding toolConfig for latLng must not pull one in.
- The snake_case cases pin GoogleSearch.UnmarshalJSON's alias handling: time_range_filter on Gemini, exclude_domains + time_range_filter together on Vertex.
- The fidelity cases pin what must survive the four conversions: webSearchQueries, a citable uri on every grounding chunk, searchEntryPoint.renderedContent (Google requires rendering Search Suggestions), and groundingSupports[].groundingChunkIndices that stay in-bounds and de-duplicated.

Each case runs on both providers via the provider-prefixed model form (/genai/v1beta/models/gemini/... and /genai/v1beta/models/vertex/...), so PROVIDER=gemini and PROVIDER=vertex both exercise the full set against their own backend.

Not covered here: googleSearch.searchTypes (Grounding with Google Image Search) and the imageSearchQueries / groundingChunks[].image response half. Those need an image model and are deferred - Bifrost currently also drops the generated inlineData part in streaming, because processGeminiPart matches part.ThoughtSignature before part.InlineData and consumes an image part carrying a thought signature as a signature-only reasoning item.

The chunk-index test checks in-bounds and de-duplicated indices; it cannot by itself catch a regression that keeps only the first index of a multi-source support, since one index is still valid. Folder 32 pins that fan-out on /v1/responses.
